published_prior_art.cite: KroftMourifieVayalinkal2024: Lemma 3 sharply characterizes response-type probabilities under researcher-chosen restrictions; the Cartesian diagonal projection is a plausible specialized transport refinement.

KroftMourifieVayalinkal2024 gives multilayer response-type/LCDE bounds, Kallus2022Harm gives sharp factual-marginal harm bounds, and neither inspected result gives the stated joint stayer--harm prism.

PossebomRiva2025 covers a binary always-observed probability-of-causation target and Kallus2022Harm covers population FNA; neither subsumes a ratio among multilayer same-layer stayers with both numerator and denominator unidentified.
PossebomRiva2025 gives binary-selection sharp probability-of-causation bounds; this observable positivity condition is a useful but algebraic corollary of the proposed endpoint formula.

soundness_flags.label: ass:ordered-selection
soundness_flags.one_line: Kroft--Mourifie--Vayalinkal call D1>=D0 an optional researcher-imposed “Strong Monotonicity” response-type restriction, not their standard multilayer selection assumption, so the present standard tag/name and citation overstate its status.

soundness_flags.label: ass:ordered-selection
soundness_flags.one_line: The load-bearing no-downward-move restriction is materially stronger than ordinary Lee monotonicity and has no application-specific justification establishing that ordered firm/layer movement is one-sided.

soundness_flags.label: symbol mu and definitions def:observable-domain / def:ambient-endpoint-map
soundness_flags.one_line: The core repeatedly uses mu(P) and calls mu an arm-cell vector, but never defines its coordinates as conditional probabilities under P; add that map explicitly.

soundness_flags.label: ass:layer-consistency and ass:outcome-consistency
soundness_flags.one_line: Both conditions already follow identically from the definition of W as the observed coarsening of potential variables, so they do not restrict M_L and should be observation-map conventions rather than model-class assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Lemma 3 gives the sharp response-type set under Assumption 1 and a chosen RT; Remark 2 labels D1>=D0 as optional “Strong Monotonicity,” whereas the paper's Assumption 2 is only binary positive-selection monotonicity 1{D1>0}>=1{D0>0}.
Theorem 2 gives a sharp interval for the fraction negatively affected under factual treatment-arm marginals, with binary all-0-to-all-1 specialization in equation (5).
Under random assignment, positive mass, and monotone binary sample selection, Proposition 2 gives sharp conditional probability-of-causation bounds for the always-observed subgroup.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag ordered selection as a novel strong-monotonicity restriction and supply a concrete setting, layer ordering, and empirical/design rationale; otherwise weaken the headline to the ordinary Lee monotonicity regime.
Define mu_z(d,y)=P(W=(z,d,y)|Z=z) and mu_z(0-star)=P(D=0|Z=z), then move consistency from M_L into the observed-data coarsening definition.

Add a direct comparison theorem showing exactly how the strong-monotonicity response-type class sits inside Kroft--Mourifie--Vayalinkal's RT formulation and why their weighted-LCDE optimizer does not yield the prism or ratio endpoints.

recommended_next_step: Revise the load-bearing ordering assumption and observable-law map, then retain the field-tier joint-prism identification kernel for Stage 0.
